Definition: a manner (as a sort of turn)
BiblicalUsage: A manner, a turn, a way of going on — that is what this word means. David says God has spoken of his house for a great while to come, and has regarded him according to the estate of a man of high degree, and the same phrase returns in Samuel's account of the same promise.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is about the shape of a life: David looks at the manner of man God has made him, and finds it more than he asked.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
